
{{alias}}( x, value[, start[, end]][, options] )
    Fills an input ndarray with a specified value along an ndarray dimension.

    When a `start` and/or `end` index is negative, the respective index is
    determined relative to the last indexed element, with out-of-bounds indices
    clamped to index bounds.

    The function fills an input ndarray in-place and thus mutates an input
    ndarray.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x: ndarray
        Input array.

    value: ndarray|any
        Fill value. May be either a scalar value or an ndarray. Must be able to
        safely cast to the input ndarray data type. Values having floating-point
        data types (both real and complex) are allowed to downcast to a lower
        precision data type of the same kind (e.g., a scalar double-precision
        floating-point number can be used to fill a 'float32' input ndarray). If
        provided an ndarray, the value must have a shape which is broadcast
        compatible with the complement of the shape defined by `options.dim`.
        For example, given the input shape `[2, 3, 4]` and `options.dim=0`, an
        ndarray fill value must have a shape which is broadcast compatible with
        the shape `[3, 4]`.

    start: ndarray|integer (optional)
        Starting index (inclusive). May be either an integer or an ndarray
        having an integer index or "generic" data type and following the same
        broadcasting semantics as an ndarray `value` argument. Default: `0`.

    end: ndarray|integer (optional)
        Ending index (exclusive). May be either an integer or an ndarray having
        an integer index or "generic" data type and following the same
        broadcasting semantics as an ndarray `value` argument. Default: `N`
        where `N` is the number of elements along the operation dimension.

    options: Object (optional)
        Function options.

    options.dim: integer (optional)
        Dimension over which to perform operation. If provided a negative
        integer, the dimension along which to perform the operation is
        determined by counting backward from the last dimension (where `-1`
        refers to the last dimension). Default: `-1`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        Input array.

    Examples
    --------
    > var x = {{alias:@stdlib/ndarray/array}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var y = {{alias}}( x, 10.0, 2 )
    <ndarray>[ 1.0, 2.0, 10.0, 10.0 ]
    > var bool = ( x === y )
    true

    See Also
    --------
